problem_motivation.content: Second-harmonic generation microscopy is limited by weak signals and interpretation difficulty in multilayer systems with competing contributions.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: However, it often suffers from weak signal strength and is difficult to understand in multilayer systems where many materials can give competing signal contributions.

problem_motivation.content: Using propagating surface plasmons to enhance SHG remains largely unexplored.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: However, while localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) enhanced SHG has now been extensively studied, enhancing SHG via delocalized, propagating surface plasmons has remained largely unexplored [22].

problem_motivation.content: SHG signals are weak and usually detectable only near the excitation spot, limiting wide-area probing.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Firstly, SHG is a weak signal that, except with specialised set-ups optimized for a particular task (e.g. examining surface reconstruction) [8], can only be detected from a region close to the (sub-micron) excitation spot on a sample surface at any time, limiting its application for understanding wide sample regions.

problem_motivation.content: In multilayer structures, multiple interfaces contribute to SHG, making competing contributions hard to separate.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Secondly, when light is incident on a multilayer structure (for example a solar cell or battery) every interface and non-centrosymmetric (and possible other weak bulk effects [23]) can contribute to the SHG, making it challenging to disentangle competing contributions.

problem_motivation.content: For multilayer structures, it is difficult to determine which interfaces generate the SHG signal.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: While SHG is a powerful probe for studying single interfaces, in multilayer structures it can be challenging to assess which interfaces contribute to the signal, as noted above.

prior_approach.content: Localized SHG enhanced by localized surface plasmon resonances has been widely studied.
prior_approach.evidence_span: However, while localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) enhanced SHG has now been extensively studied, enhancing SHG via delocalized, propagating surface plasmons has remained largely unexplored [22].

prior_approach.content: SPPs are typically excited using either Kretschmann configuration or gratings to supply momentum.
prior_approach.evidence_span: SPPs, being evanescent surface waves, do not directly couple to the optical beams incident from the surroundings due to momentum mismatch, so their excitation is typically achieved via Kretschmann-type configuration or through employing a grating to provide additional momentum to the incident beam [30].

prior_approach.content: Previous work showed dielectric layers on metals can enhance SHG via more favorable Fresnel coefficients.
prior_approach.evidence_span: SHG has been previously shown to be enhanced by dielectric layers on metals due to more favourable Fresnel reflection/transmission coefficients at interfaces [36].

prior_approach.content: This polarization behavior had been previously observed in local SHG measurements on {111} monocrystalline gold.
prior_approach.evidence_span: This has previously been observed in local SHG measurements on {111} monocrystalline gold surfaces

prior_approach.content: Gold flake synthesis followed an existing published chemical synthesis method.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Chemical synthesis procedure followed the same methodology as described elsewhere [44,45].

prior_approach.content: Grating design followed a previously published approach.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Gratings were designed following the approach outlined in [30].

prior_approach.content: Grating depth choice was based on previous studies.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Based on previous studies [46] we chose the depth of the etched part of the gratings to be approximately 70 nm

causal_claim.content: The results show SPP-induced SHG can serve as a surface probe of buried interfaces while addressing weak and localized SHG limitations.

causal_claim.content: Interference of the two counter-propagating, interface-confined SPPs produces SHG observable in the far field.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This implies that the interference of the two counter-propagating SPPs, which are confined at the interface at the fundamental frequency, results in SHG that is observable in the far-field

causal_claim.content: Using two counter-propagating SPPs enables conversion of an evanescent wave into a free-space propagating SHG wave, unlike a single SPP.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Thus, we demonstrate not only spatial decoupling of the SHG and fundamental signals on the surface, but also conversion of the intrinsically evanescent wave to a free-space propagating wave, which is not attainable with a single SPP, as demonstrated above.

causal_claim.content: Isolating SHG from only the interface of interest enables nonlinear imaging without broad illumination.
causal_claim.evidence_span: While ensuring that the SHG signal originates solely from the interface of interest, this also enables the possibility of non-linear imaging without the need for a broad laser illumination area.

causal_claim.content: The observed SHG fringes arise from interference between SPP-induced SHG and SHG from the gratings.
causal_claim.evidence_span: We present a thorough investigation of these features in Supplementary Information Note 7, demonstrating that they originate from interference of the SPP-induced SHG and SHG originating from the gratings

causal_claim.content: The polarization behavior shows that the SHG is generated by a nonlinear susceptibility component sensitive to the crystal facet.

causal_claim.content: The study concludes that in-plane second-order susceptibility components dominate the SHG response in this case.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Therefore, we have shown that in-plane components of the second-order susceptibility tensor dominate the SHG response in this case, which is also consistent with the previous reports.

causal_claim.content: Their results enable or open possibilities for enhanced delocalized SHG and other nonlinear effects across buried interfaces, supporting applications in multilayers, surface science, and bioimaging.
causal_claim.evidence_span: We believe that our results open new possibilities in fundamental and applied research, demonstrating possibilities for delocalized enhancement of SHG and other nonlinear effects across buried interfaces, and paving the way to wide variety of applications including in multilayer structures for energy applications, surface science and biological imaging.

causal_claim.evidence_span: Thus a single SPP can never produce far-field SHG, unless it can outcouple via other momentum-matching mechanism such as grating coupling (e.g. Kretschmann configuration).

mechanism_principle.content: Local electric field enhancements are offered as part of the reason the signals could be observed easily.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: In part due to local electric field enhancements, we were able to observe these signals on a CMOS camera with 1 s exposure and no gain using an industrial-grade pulsed laser.

mechanism_principle.content: The authors attribute further enhancement to stronger vertical SPP confinement, higher electric field amplitude, and refraction at the SiO2 interface, with susceptibility changes also likely relevant.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Here we suggest further improvements are due to increased SPP vertical confinement, and hence the electric field amplitude, and  refraction at the SiO2 interface ensuring more of the beam is incident close to perpendicular to the in-coupling grating, though note that changes to the effective nonlinear susceptibility components are likely also important [37,38].

mechanism_principle.content: The normal-direction emission suggests k-space restrictions govern formation of SPP-induced SHG.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This is suggestive of k-space restrictions on how SPP-induced SHG is formed.

mechanism_principle.content: Because the squared sum of counter-propagating SPP fields contains an x-independent term at 2ω, it corresponds to a plane wave normal to the surface.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: As SHG is proportional to the electric field squared (i.e. (𝐸SPP,1 + 𝐸SPP,2)2), for two counter-propagating SPPs this expression contains a term that is constant in 𝑥 ... An optical electric field at frequency 2𝜔 which is constant in amplitude as position is varied across the sample surface is, by definition, a plane wave perpendicular to the sample surface.

mechanism_principle.content: The model indicates the SHG comes from an in-plane nonlinear polarization component, not the out-of-plane one.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Our model reveals that the nonlinear polarisation component responsible for the SHG must be an in-plane polarisation (in this situation 𝑃⃑ x, see discussion below), while the out-of-plane polarisation cannot contribute to this phenomenon.

mechanism_principle.content: The grating-originated SHG contributes far from the gratings because of the microscope's finite numerical aperture.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: which has a small component far from the gratings due to the finite numerical aperture of the microscope.

mechanism_principle.content: A {111} monocrystalline gold surface has extra anisotropic second-order susceptibility elements because its symmetry is c3v rather than the isotropic c∞ case.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Importantly, in comparison with an isotropic surface (e.g. evaporated or sputtered polycrystalline films), a {111}-type crystalline gold surface features additional anisotropic elements of the second-order susceptibility tensor 𝜒⃡(2). This is due to isotropic surfaces having 𝑐∞ symmetry, whereas {111}-type surface belongs to 𝑐3𝑣 symmetry group [37,42].

mechanism_principle.content: For isotropic surfaces, only surface-normal fields produce SHG, while {111} surfaces also allow in-plane-field-driven SHG because inversion symmetry is broken in-plane.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Hence, in the case of an isotropic surface, only interaction with a surface-normal polarized optical field would result in SHG, since the inversion symmetry is broken only across the interface. In turn, {111}-type surface additionally has broken inversion symmetry in-plane, and thus possess additional  𝜒⃡(2)tensor elements that also interact with surface-parallel polarized optical field.

mechanism_principle.content: Matching grating spatial frequency to the SPP enables normal-incidence light to diffract into the SPP mode.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Specifically, the grating period was chosen to have the same spatial frequency as a surface plasmon polariton travelling along the surface of a gold flake. Thus, when a beam is incident perpendicular to the structure it is diffracted directly into an SPP channel.

mechanism_principle.content: The poorer convergence is explained by discontinuities in the tangential electric-field derivative at sharp grating edges.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: this method exhibits worse numerical convergence, as calculation of the nonlinear polarization involves tangential derivative of the electric field, which has abrupt discontinuity at the sharp features of the grating structure.

mechanism_principle.content: The broadband response is explained by the gratings being square and thus containing many optical frequencies.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: We attribute this to our gratings being square, meaning they include many optical frequencies.

mechanism_principle.content: The reduced power flow and increased amplitude are explained by partial SPP reflection producing a partial standing wave.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This is explained by a significant portion of the SPP being reflected by the grating, reducing the time averaged power flow while increasing the field amplitude (i.e. a partial standing wave).

mechanism_principle.content: Single-SPP SHG cannot radiate to free space because the relevant wavevector component is complex rather than real.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Importantly, 𝜖m, the permittivity of the metal is always a complex number whose real part is less than -1 at optical frequencies, meaning that 𝑞1 is a complex number. In other words SHG from a single SPP cannot couple to free-space as free-space wave-vectors are always real.

mechanism_principle.content: Because the emitted wavevector is normal to the surface, the emitted electric field cannot have a z component.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: As we have just shown 𝑘⃑ ̂1 = (0 0 1), this in turn means that 𝐸⃑ 𝑛𝑙 can have no 𝑧 component (this is clear as no plane wave can have an electric field component in the direction of travel).

mechanism_principle.content: A likely alternative source is grating-generated SHG, which is stronger and emitted over many angles.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Specifically, we note that SHG stronger than that from the SPPs is produced at the gratings (at either end of the SPP induced SHG) and, furthermore, the oscillations are largest closest to these gratings... SHG from the gratings, unlike that from the SPP induced SHG, is emitted over a wide range of angles

hypothesis_statement.content: The authors believe this is the first microscale observation of this process.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: which we believe to be the first observation of this process at the microscale

hypothesis_statement.content: The authors claim this is the first experimental demonstration of delocalized SPP-induced SHG over more than 10 μm.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: To the best of our knowledge, we report the first experimental demonstration of SPP-induced SHG with delocalization over > 10 m length scales.

hypothesis_statement.content: The authors believe this is a novel report of SHG increasing with distance from the excitation spot and the first delocalized SPP-induced surface SHG from a wide buried planar interface.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: We believe this to be a novel report of SHG signal increasing in strength away from the excitation spot, and, importantly, the first report of spatially delocalized, SPP-induced surface-SHG from a wide (tens of micrometers) planar buried interface.

hypothesis_statement.content: The authors believe this is the first observation of such a signal at the microscale.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: We believe this to be the first time such signal has been observed at the microscale.

hypothesis_statement.content: They propose that grating-emitted wide-angle SHG, observed away from the grating peak, interferes with SPP-induced SHG to create the oscillations.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: We propose that this is the situation in our experiments i.e. SHG is produced at a wide range of angles from the gratings. When we observe a region away from the grating peak, the grating gives small contributions to the signal at angles close to the maximum observed value of k-space. The interference of this signal with the SPP induced SHG results in the oscillations observed in our measurement

evidence_result.content: The study observed second-harmonic light generated far from the excitation spot.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We generate second-harmonic light up to 35 µm from the excitation spot

evidence_result.content: The study obtained signal from atomically flat surfaces without the fundamental beam in the same region.
evidence_result.evidence_span: we obtain signal from atomically flat surfaces without a fundamental excitation beam present in the same region

evidence_result.content: The emitted signal shows the same polarisation dependence as localised second-harmonic generation and forms a collimated beam normal to the surface.
evidence_result.evidence_span: This signal has the same polarisation dependence as localised second-harmonic generation and is emitted in a collimated beam travelling perpendicular to the sample surface.

evidence_result.content: The signals were detectable on a CMOS camera with short exposure and no gain using an industrial-grade pulsed laser.
evidence_result.evidence_span: we were able to observe these signals on a CMOS camera with 1 s exposure and no gain using an industrial-grade pulsed laser

evidence_result.content: Plasmon-enhanced SHG was observed up to 35 μm from the excitation spot across monocrystalline gold.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Plasmon-enhanced SHG is observed as far as 35 m away from the excitation spot and generated across a monocrystalline gold surface.

evidence_result.content: High signal strength allowed SHG imaging with a low-cost CMOS camera and low-energy industrial pulsed laser.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The high signal strength allowed us to observe SHG light using a low-cost CMOS camera with 1 s exposure times and an industrial-grade pulsed laser with ~ 1 nJ per pulse (40 MHz repetition rate, <200 fs pulse width).

evidence_result.content: The gratings behaved as intended, producing visible out-coupled signal at the second grating.
evidence_result.evidence_span: As shown in Figure 1c, the gratings function as expected: illumination of the in-coupling grating (bright spot on the left-hand side) results in a visible signal at the out-coupling grating (two stripes on the right-hand side).

evidence_result.content: Absorption measurements suggest up to 20% of incident power couples into an SPP.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We also carried out absorption measurements which suggest up to 20 % of the incident power couples to a surface-plasmon-polariton, as discussed in Supplementary Information Note 1.

evidence_result.content: The observed signal was verified as SHG by spectrum and quadratic power scaling.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We confirmed the observed signal was SHG through both its spectrum and quadratic scaling with incident fundamental laser beam power (Supplementary Information Note 2).

evidence_result.content: A weaker but clear SHG signal appeared at the outcoupling grating, delocalized from the excitation position.
evidence_result.evidence_span: A weaker SHG signal is also clearly seen at the outcoupling grating, i.e. the signal is delocalized with respect to the excitation position, with total counts 0.5 % of the intensity of the SHG at the excitation spot, which can be clearly seen in a line profile presented in Figure 1e.

evidence_result.content: No SHG was detected from the planar gold surface between gratings in the single-SPP configuration.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Importantly, this plot also reveals that no SHG signal was detected from the planar gold surface between the gratings

evidence_result.content: The SHG mainly originates from grating ridges, matching prior theoretical expectations.
evidence_result.evidence_span: the SHG originates mostly from the ridges of the two gratings, in qualitative accordance with the previous theoretical considerations [34].

evidence_result.content: Comparable SHG results were reproduced across three nonlinear microscope setups.
evidence_result.evidence_span: To confirm our results we repeated this SHG measurements on three different nonlinear microscope setups and saw comparable results in all cases (see Methods).

evidence_result.content: Comparable results were obtained for grating spacings from 10 to 35 μm.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We also explored different grating spacings and saw comparable results for all grating spacings explored (10 – 35 µm).

evidence_result.content: Finite element modeling confirmed the second grating acts as a reflector with about 33% SPP power reflection.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We confirmed this second grating acts as a reflector using finite element method modelling, see Supplementary Information Note 3, with our simulations indicating approximately 33 % of the SPP’s power is reflected at 1030 nm.

evidence_result.content: With counter-propagating SPPs, SHG emission was detected from the unpatterned surface between the gratings.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Excitingly, in addition to the SHG signal from the two gratings, similar to the described-above measurements, we detect SHG emission from the unpatterned surface between them.

evidence_result.content: There was no significant fundamental emission from the region between gratings aside from minor speckles.
evidence_result.evidence_span: At the same time, we do not observe any significant fundamental beam emission from the region between the two gratings, apart from some minor speckles due to the scattering of the excitation laser beam.

evidence_result.content: Across the unpatterned region, SHG stayed above 30% while the fundamental dropped below 5% within a few microns.
evidence_result.evidence_span: While the fundamental signal drops to less than 5 % of this maximum just a few microns away from the grating, the SHG signal remains larger than 30 % of the maximum across the entire unpatterned region.

evidence_result.content: Similar counter-propagating-SPP SHG results were observed for reflector spacings from 10 to 35 μm.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We observe similar results for reflection gratings spaced from 10 µm to 35 µm from the in-coupling grating, as is presented in Supplementary Information Note 4.

evidence_result.content: The strongest SHG in the buried-interface sample occurred at the reflection grating 20 μm away, and the signal was visible across the whole region.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Remarkably, the SHG signal is clearly visible over the entire region of interest even on a linear scale and the strongest SHG signal is now observed at the reflection grating (Figure 2i), located 20 μm away.

evidence_result.content: Adding SiO2 significantly enhanced SHG, about fivefold in intensity between gratings, enabling imaging with an inexpensive color CMOS camera.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We also note that all SHG signals were significantly enhanced relative to those in air (for the region between the gratings, approximately by a factor of 5 in intensity), to the point that we could record the image in Figure 2i using an inexpensive colour CMOS microscopy camera with 1 s exposure time.

evidence_result.content: For bare gold and grating excitation, SHG was emitted over a wide range of angles; for between-grating detection it was centered near normal emission.
evidence_result.evidence_span: For case i. and ii. we observe contributions to the SHG signal at a wide range of angles... Conversely, for case iii. the SHG signal is concentrated around the centre of the back-focal-plane, indicating that SPP-induced SHG is preferentially emitted perpendicular to the gold surface

evidence_result.content: The analytical model predicts SHG from a single SPP remains evanescent and does not outcouple to the far field.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Briefly, we find that for a single SPP any SHG waves that are produced remain evanescent, i.e. they do not outcouple from the surface to the far field.

evidence_result.content: Simulations show that without a reflection grating, SHG reaches the far field only at gratings; with a reflector, SHG also emerges across the unpatterned surface normal to the surface.
evidence_result.evidence_span: For the case without a reflection grating, SHG only couples to the far-field at the gratings, comparable to the fundamental beam. Conversely, when a reflection grating is present (Figure 3f), SHG is produced both at the gratings ... and, importantly, across the entire unpatterned monocrystalline surface, where the beam is emitted only in the surface-normal direction.

evidence_result.content: Additional simulations confirmed that one SPP does not couple to far-field SHG, whereas two counter-propagating SPPs do.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We further confirmed our model by simulating a single SPP travelling across a monocrystalline surface and observed no coupling to far-field SHG, while two counter-propagating SPPs do couple to far-field SHG

evidence_result.content: For gratings parallel to the crystal edge, SHG polarization followed the same dependence as the fundamental; for perpendicular gratings, the SHG was cross-polarized.
evidence_result.evidence_span: For the grating parallel to the crystal edge, the SHG polarisation follows the same polarisation dependence as the fundamental beam (Figure 4b, red circles). However, for the gratings perpendicular to the crystal edge the SHG beam is cross-polarized with respect to the fundamental beam (Figure 4c, red circles).

evidence_result.content: Based on measurements and modeling, the authors assign the signals to χxxx(2) and χxyy(2) for the two grating orientations.

problem_motivation.content: Second-harmonic generation microscopy is limited by weak signal strength, which is typically only detectable near the sub-micron excitation spot and thus restricts wide-area probing.
evidence_spans: However, it often suffers from weak signal strength and is difficult to understand in multilayer systems where many materials can give competing signal contributions.

Firstly, SHG is a weak signal that, except with specialised set-ups optimized for a particular task (e.g. examining surface reconstruction) [8], can only be detected from a region close to the (sub-micron) excitation spot on a sample surface at any time, limiting its application for understanding wide sample regions.

problem_motivation.content: In multilayer structures, SHG interpretation is difficult because multiple interfaces/materials can contribute competing signals, making it hard to disentangle which interfaces generate the observed SHG.
evidence_spans: However, it often suffers from weak signal strength and is difficult to understand in multilayer systems where many materials can give competing signal contributions.

Secondly, when light is incident on a multilayer structure (for example a solar cell or battery) every interface and non-centrosymmetric (and possible other weak bulk effects [23]) can contribute to the SHG, making it challenging to disentangle competing contributions.
While SHG is a powerful probe for studying single interfaces, in multilayer structures it can be challenging to assess which interfaces contribute to the signal, as noted above.

mechanism_principle.content: Because the emitted SHG wavevector is normal to the surface, the emitted electric field cannot have a z component; accordingly, the responsible nonlinear polarization must be in-plane (here Px), while the out-of-plane polarization cannot contribute.

mechanism_principle.content: A {111} monocrystalline gold surface has additional anisotropic second-order susceptibility tensor elements because its symmetry is c3v rather than the isotropic c∞ case; therefore isotropic surfaces allow SHG only from surface-normal fields, whereas {111} surfaces also allow in-plane-field-driven SHG because inversion symmetry is broken in-plane.
evidence_spans: Importantly, in comparison with an isotropic surface (e.g. evaporated or sputtered polycrystalline films), a {111}-type crystalline gold surface features additional anisotropic elements of the second-order susceptibility tensor 𝜒⃡(2). This is due to isotropic surfaces having 𝑐∞ symmetry, whereas {111}-type surface belongs to 𝑐3𝑣 symmetry group [37,42].

Hence, in the case of an isotropic surface, only interaction with a surface-normal polarized optical field would result in SHG, since the inversion symmetry is broken only across the interface. In turn, {111}-type surface additionally has broken inversion symmetry in-plane, and thus possess additional  𝜒⃡(2)tensor elements that also interact with surface-parallel polarized optical field.

evidence_result.evidence_span: While the fundamental signal drops to less than 5 % of this maximum just a few microns away from the grating, the SHG signal remains larger than 30 % of the maximum across the entire unpatterned region.

evidence_result.content: Similar counter-propagating-SPP SHG results were observed for reflector spacings from 10 to 35 μm.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We observe similar results for reflection gratings spaced from 10 µm to 35 µm from the in-coupling grating, as is presented in Supplementary Information Note 4.

evidence_result.content: The strongest SHG in the buried-interface sample occurred at the reflection grating 20 μm away, and the signal was visible across the whole region.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Remarkably, the SHG signal is clearly visible over the entire region of interest even on a linear scale and the strongest SHG signal is now observed at the reflection grating (Figure 2i), located 20 μm away.

evidence_result.content: Adding SiO2 significantly enhanced SHG, about fivefold in intensity between gratings, enabling imaging with an inexpensive color CMOS camera.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We also note that all SHG signals were significantly enhanced relative to those in air (for the region between the gratings, approximately by a factor of 5 in intensity), to the point that we could record the image in Figure 2i using an inexpensive colour CMOS microscopy camera with 1 s exposure time.

evidence_result.content: For bare gold and grating excitation, SHG was emitted over a wide range of angles; for between-grating detection it was centered near normal emission.
evidence_result.evidence_span: For case i. and ii. we observe contributions to the SHG signal at a wide range of angles... Conversely, for case iii. the SHG signal is concentrated around the centre of the back-focal-plane, indicating that SPP-induced SHG is preferentially emitted perpendicular to the gold surface

evidence_result.content: The analytical model predicts SHG from a single SPP remains evanescent and does not outcouple to the far field.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Briefly, we find that for a single SPP any SHG waves that are produced remain evanescent, i.e. they do not outcouple from the surface to the far field.

evidence_result.content: Simulations show that without a reflection grating, SHG reaches the far field only at gratings; with a reflector, SHG also emerges across the unpatterned surface normal to the surface.
evidence_result.evidence_span: For the case without a reflection grating, SHG only couples to the far-field at the gratings, comparable to the fundamental beam. Conversely, when a reflection grating is present (Figure 3f), SHG is produced both at the gratings ... and, importantly, across the entire unpatterned monocrystalline surface, where the beam is emitted only in the surface-normal direction.

evidence_result.content: Additional simulations confirmed that one SPP does not couple to far-field SHG, whereas two counter-propagating SPPs do.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We further confirmed our model by simulating a single SPP travelling across a monocrystalline surface and observed no coupling to far-field SHG, while two counter-propagating SPPs do couple to far-field SHG

evidence_result.content: For gratings parallel to the crystal edge, SHG polarization followed the same dependence as the fundamental; for perpendicular gratings, the SHG was cross-polarized.
evidence_result.evidence_span: For the grating parallel to the crystal edge, the SHG polarisation follows the same polarisation dependence as the fundamental beam (Figure 4b, red circles). However, for the gratings perpendicular to the crystal edge the SHG beam is cross-polarized with respect to the fundamental beam (Figure 4c, red circles).

evidence_result.content: Based on measurements and modeling, the authors assign the signals to χxxx(2) and χxyy(2) for the two grating orientations.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Based on these results and our modelling (see Supplementary Information Note 6), we identify that our signals are due to 𝜒𝑥𝑥𝑥(2) and 𝜒xyy(2)  for SPPs launched by gratings parallel to and perpendicular to a crystal edges respectively

evidence_result.content: They demonstrated delocalized SHG up to 35 μm from the excitation beam via SPP coupling.
evidence_result.evidence_span: we have demonstrated delocalized SHG at up to 35 m from the excitation beam by coupling the fundamental beam to SPPs

evidence_result.content: They observed SHG generation from a flat monocrystalline surface with little far-field fundamental emission through two counter-propagating SPPs.
evidence_result.evidence_span: we reveal that SHG can be generated from a flat monocrystalline surface, with minimal concurrent far-field fundamental emission, through the interaction of two counter-propagating SPPs

evidence_result.content: The emitted SHG is highly directional, normal to the interface, and its polarization depends on local crystal structure.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We show that emitted SHG from the monocrystalline surface is highly directional, propagating perpendicular to the interface only, and that the polarisation of this signal is sensitive to the local crystal structure.

evidence_result.content: The signal can originate from a single buried interface in a multilayer and be recorded with low-cost instrumentation and short exposure.
evidence_result.evidence_span: we demonstrate that this signal can arise from a single buried interface within a multilayer structure and can be recorded with an inexpensive CMOS camera, industrial-grade laser and reasonable (~1 s) exposure times.

evidence_result.content: Repeating part of the experiments on two other nonlinear microscopes gave qualitatively similar results, though intensities and fringe periods differed.
evidence_result.evidence_span: A portion of experiments were repeated on two different nonlinear microscopy setups, equipped with a Ti:Saph and Mai-Tai lasers both operating at 820 nm and 1030 nm respectively. The obtained results were qualitatively similar, although with different relative intensities and different fringe periodicities were observed in the counter-propagating SPP experiments.

evidence_result.content: They validated the surface-SHG simulation approach by reproducing expected angular distributions for a Gaussian beam and different susceptibility terms.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We confirmed that this approach produced surface-based second-harmonic generation results correctly prior to applying it to our application: we showed that a Gaussian beam focused on the surface produced the expected angular distribution of SHG for different nonlinear susceptibility terms.

evidence_result.content: An additional simulation excluding gratings from the nonlinear layer confirmed perpendicular SHG emission from the region between gratings for the ExEx case.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We further confirmed that the region between the gratings gives SHG emitted perpendicular to the surface for the P⃑ x nls ∝ ExEx option by carrying out a second simulation in which we excluded the gratings from the nonlinear polarisation layer above the gold, and our results are fully consistent with results in this text.

evidence_result.content: Measurements showed broadband reflection reduction from about 700 to 1100 nm for perpendicular polarization.
evidence_result.evidence_span: More specifically, our measurements show a broadband reduction in reflection between ~700 nm and ~ 1100 nm, compared to the parallel polarisation case.

evidence_result.content: At 1030 nm, up to about 20% of incident light coupled into SPPs.
evidence_result.evidence_span: At this wavelength, our measurements suggest up to 20 % of the incident beam couples to surface plasmon polaritons.

evidence_result.content: Spectral and power-dependent measurements confirmed the detected signal was SHG.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We confirmed we are observing second-harmonic generation through spectral and power-dependant measurements, as presented in Figure S2.

evidence_result.content: Both regions showed a strong 515 nm peak and weak broad two-photon photoluminescence at longer wavelengths.
evidence_result.evidence_span: It can be seen both signals have a strong peak at the SHG wavelength (515 nm) and a weak and broad two-photon photoluminescence signal at longer wavelengths, consistent with previous reports [2].

evidence_result.content: Power scaling was quadratic with coefficient 1.95, confirming SHG.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We fit with a straight line and obtain a coefficient of 1.95 i.e. implying counts are quadratic with laser power, confirming SHG.

evidence_result.content: Introducing the reflection grating increased field amplitude before the grating.
evidence_result.evidence_span: By comparing Figure S3a (no grating) and b (with grating), the electric field amplitude prior to the gratings (noting SPPs are incident from the left side of the simulation) is seen to increase in the latter case.

evidence_result.content: Adding the grating reduced forward power flow by 30–40%.
evidence_result.evidence_span: When the grating is introduced we observe a reduction in the power flow (a reduction of 30-40 %).

evidence_result.content: Simulations estimated that about 33% of SPP power was reflected backward by the grating.
evidence_result.evidence_span: we were able to calculate that approximately 33 % of the power is reflected into a backwards propagating SPP by the grating.

evidence_result.content: Structures with grating spacings from 10 to 35 µm gave qualitatively similar SHG results.
evidence_result.evidence_span: As can be seen, we observe qualitatively similar results in all cases.

evidence_result.content: COMSOL showed single-SPP excitation gives only extremely weak far-field SHG, mainly from simulation edges.
evidence_result.evidence_span: As expected, for a single SPP we see extremely weak coupling to far-field SHG, primarily arising from the simulation edges (i.e. the gold/matched layer boundary).

evidence_result.content: COMSOL showed counter-propagating SPPs give strong far-field SHG from the full surface with wavevector normal to the surface.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Conversely, for two counter-propagating SPPs we observe strong coupling to far-field SHG arising from the entire gold surface, and that this radiation’s k-vector is perpendicular to the gold surface.

evidence_result.content: The flat-surface SHG oscillations were a small fraction of the total signal, typically below 20%.
evidence_result.evidence_span: This was always a small component of the total signal, typically less than 20 %.

evidence_result.content: Fringe spacing depended on objective NA: 0.78 µm at NA 0.7, 0.64 µm at 0.75, and 1.13 µm at 0.45.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Rather, we find that the spacing of the fringes is 0.78 µm for NA of 0.7, but changes with objective NA (0.64 µm/1.13 µm for NA of 0.75/0.45).

evidence_result.content: The measured fringe spacing matched that expected when the high-angle wave was at the objective's maximum angle.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The measured spacing of the fringes (i.e. 𝑎 on Figure S7b) matched that observed when the high angle wave is incident with the maximum angle (NA) allowed by our objective, confirming that the real-space oscillations are due to the interaction of these two plane waves.

evidence_result.content: Reducing the range of incident angles with an iris reduced oscillation spacing, indicating a high-angle SHG background contributes.
evidence_result.evidence_span: As the range of incident angles is reduced, the spacing of the oscillations reduces i.e. there is a small background SHG component at several angles, and the highest angle component produces the oscillations that we observe.

evidence_result.content: Back-focal-plane measurements near an incoupling grating without reflection grating still showed strong signal at the maximum angular extent.
evidence_result.evidence_span: We again observe strong signal contributions at the maximum spatial extent of the back-focal-plane, as is presented in Figure S9c.

constraint.content: The random nature of the synthesis produces many different gold crystal types, so only large, clean, undamaged flakes could be selected and used for subsequent FIB patterning.
evidence_spans: Due to random nature of the synthesis process, a large variety of gold crystals are created in every synthesis batch and only the large, clean and undamaged samples are selected for subsequent patterning using FIB.

constraint.content: The optical beam was constrained to fill the central portion of the back focal plane because the gratings couple most effectively for near-normal (approximately perpendicular) incidence.
evidence_spans: we used a Gaussian shaped beam with a spot radius of 3 ± 0.2 µm that filled the central portion of the back-focal-plane (as gratings couple most effectively to light incident perpendicular to the sample)

contradiction.content: The observed fringe spacing did not match the SPP wavelength or a frequency-doubled SPP.
evidence_spans: We recorded the spacing of the real space oscillations, which did not correspond to the wavelength of the SPP nor a frequency doubled SPP.
